items.title: 12.2.3 Synthesis of ammonia from ammonium salts

source_refs.note: Topic 12.2.3 with Figure 12.3 and Quick Check 12.1, printed page 275.

blocks.text: In the laboratory, ammonia gas can be synthesized by heating an ammonium salt such as ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl) with a base like calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂) as shown in Figure 12.3.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: There is no sodium in the reactants, so NaCl cannot form; calcium chloride forms. The printed equation is also not balanced. The balanced equation is 2NH₄Cl(s) + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCl₂ + 2H₂O(l) + 2NH₃(g).

In this acid-base reaction, NH₄⁺ acts as an acid by donating H⁺ ions, while OH⁻ acts as a base by accepting H⁺ ions. This reaction displaces ammonia gas from the ammonium salt and produces salt and water. It is commonly used to identify ammonium in salt analysis. If a gas with a pungent smell is released and turns moistened red litmus paper blue, it indicates the presence of ammonium in the compound.

blocks.alt: Laboratory set-up. A boiling tube holding a white solid mixture is clamped to a stand and heated at its closed end by a burner; its mouth is raised, as printed, and is closed by a cork. A delivery tube runs to the foot of a drying tower packed with white lumps. A tube from the top of the tower enters an inverted gas jar held by a second stand; arrows at the mouth of the jar show air escaping. Pointer arrows mark the mixture, the lumps and the jar.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.3: Synthesis of ammonia gas (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.3).

blocks.prompt: a) Why N₂ gas is used in food packaging?
blocks.explanation: N₂ is inert: it does not react with food. The air (oxygen and moisture) in the packet is replaced by N₂, so the food is not spoiled by oxidation, bacteria and fungi do not grow, and the cushion of gas protects items such as chips from breaking.

blocks.prompt: b) Both CO and N₂ have triple bonds in their molecules. Why do you think CO is more reactive than N₂?
blocks.explanation: In N₂ both atoms are the same, so the bond is completely non-polar. In CO, carbon and oxygen are different atoms with different electronegativities, so the molecule is polar, and carbon has a lone pair that it can easily donate to another atom (for example a metal). This polarity and the lone pair make CO more reactive.

blocks.prompt: c) Ammonium salts such as (NH₄)₂SO₄ or (NH₄)₂NO₃ are commonly used as fertilizers. Why a farmer wouldn’t treat a field with an ammonium fertilizer at the same time as using lime? What would be the chemical reactions?
blocks.explanation:
Lime (CaO or Ca(OH)₂) is a base. A base liberates ammonia gas from an ammonium salt; the ammonia escapes into the air and the nitrogen of the fertilizer is wasted:
(NH₄)₂SO₄ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaSO₄ + 2H₂O + 2NH₃
2NH₄NO₃ + Ca(OH)₂ → Ca(NO₃)₂ + 2H₂O + 2NH₃

blocks.prompt: d) If magnesium ribbon is ignited and placed in a jar containing N₂O, it continues to burn brightly. Explain this observation with reason.
blocks.explanation: The heat of the burning magnesium decomposes N₂O and releases oxygen, in which the magnesium keeps burning: Mg + N₂O → MgO + N₂. This is why Table 12.2 says that N₂O supports combustion.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Ammonium nitrate is NH₄NO₃, not (NH₄)₂NO₃: one NH₄⁺ ion balances one NO₃⁻ ion.
